title: Check yourself: Writing an MCP server: tools, resources, prompts and the stdout rule

questions.stem: A stdio server prints a debug line with the language's ordinary print function, and the client then fails to parse the stream. Why?

options.text: The client reads standard error as well, and treats any text there as fatal
options.says: Ruled out because the client "SHOULD NOT assume stderr output indicates error conditions".

options.text: Standard output carries only protocol messages, so stray text corrupts it
options.says: The page says "The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message."

options.text: The SDK forbids logging libraries, so every debug line is rejected
options.says: Ruled out because the guide says to use a logger that writes to stderr: "Never write to stdout. Writing to stdout will corrupt the JSON-RPC messages and break your server."

options.text: Printed lines are queued and delivered after the tool call has ended
options.says: Ruled out because the stream carries one message per line and "The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message", with no queue of printed lines.

questions.stem: A search tool receives a date range in the wrong format, and the server wants the model to try again with a fix. How should the failure be reported?

options.text: As a JSON-RPC error response, which is passed to the model for retries
options.says: Ruled out because "Clients MAY provide protocol errors to language models, though these are less likely to result in successful recovery."

options.text: As a protocol error that says the request itself is malformed
options.says: Ruled out because a wrong format is an "Input validation errors (e.g., date in wrong format, value out of range)", which is a tool execution error and not a malformed request.

options.text: By returning empty text, which signals the model to ask the user
options.says: Ruled out because "Clients SHOULD provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction", which needs text that says what to change.

options.text: As an ordinary result flagged as an error, with a readable explanation
options.says: The page says tool execution errors "contain actionable feedback that language models can use to self-correct and retry with adjusted parameters", and lists "Input validation errors (e.g., date in wrong format, value out of range)" among them.

questions.stem: A tool's annotations say that it only reads data, and a client skips the confirmation prompt because of them. What does the specification say about relying on them?

options.text: Follow them as binding unless the tool is marked destructive
options.says: Ruled out because annotations help a client "decide whether to ask a person", "not because they enforce anything", so no marking makes them binding.

options.text: Treat them as untrusted unless the server is trusted
options.says: The page quotes the specification: "clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers."

options.text: Follow them unless the first call ends with an error
options.says: Ruled out because trust depends on where the server comes from, "unless they come from trusted servers", and not on how a first call went.

options.text: Let the SDK verify them unless the server runs locally
options.says: Ruled out because annotations are only "Optional properties describing tool behavior", and nothing on the page says the SDK checks them, locally or not.
